outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Crypto, led by Bitcoin and Ethereum
strongest.reason: both extended their rally as the White House and crypto-industry leaders pushed hard for the Clarity Act and the Treasury's long-term debt buyback plan pulled yields lower, even though the Senate's procedural vote has slipped to a September date

strongest.area: Beaten-down enterprise software, led by Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Adobe
strongest.reason: all three have rebounded sharply over the past one to two weeks as investors rotate profits out of richly valued AI-hardware winners and into software names that had fallen 30%+ this year on AI-disruption fears

weakest.area: Chips & semiconductors broadly, led by Nvidia, AMD, TSM, and Micron
weakest.reason: the group pulled back together today, with nerves and some profit-taking ahead of Nvidia's high-stakes August 26 earnings report, the single biggest catalyst on the calendar this week

weakest.area: Robotics, led by Tesla, Teradyne, and UBTECH
weakest.reason: all three gave back ground today even as the longer-term humanoid-robotics thesis stays intact; single-name volatility in the group remains high, especially in the more speculative China-listed names

outlook.nextStep: Nvidia's August 26 earnings report and Fed Chair Warsh's August 28 Jackson Hole speech are the two dominant catalysts this week and probably deserve the closest attention across the chip, AI-infrastructure, and macro tiers. The software-sector rotation and crypto's Clarity-Act-driven gains are probably better treated as trends worth watching than as one-off events to react to before those two catalysts land.

signals.title: Bond-market anxiety builds ahead of Warsh's debut Jackson Hole speech
signals.body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole speech as chair on Friday, August 28, with traders and analysts watching closely for guidance on the recent jump in bond yields and for signs of his independence from the White House. Warsh has said he wants to wait for recommendations from five task forces established earlier this year before getting too detailed about his plans, which has left markets somewhat in the dark on the near-term rate path.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at how directly Warsh addresses the rate path Friday, given how much the bond market has been pricing in ahead of the speech

signals.title: Chips pull back together as Nvidia's August 26 earnings approach
signals.body: Nvidia, AMD, TSM, and Micron all traded lower today ahead of Nvidia's Q2 report, due after the bell on August 26. Analysts are modeling roughly $93-95B in revenue (about 95% year-over-year growth), with price targets clustering between $275 and $325. The pullback looks like pre-earnings positioning rather than a reaction to fresh negative news.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether Wednesday's results confirm the AI-infrastructure demand story or reignite the ROI-fear narrative from earlier this summer

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum extend their Clarity Act-driven rally, but the Senate vote has slipped again
signals.body: Bitcoin surged past $78,000 last week for a roughly 22.6% weekly rally as President Trump and crypto-industry executives made a last-ditch push for the Clarity Act, and both Bitcoin and Ethereum have continued to grind higher since. A decline in long-term Treasury yields, following the Treasury's announcement that it would double long-term debt buybacks, has also supported the move. The Senate's procedural vote on the bill, however, has been pushed to September.
signals.focus: worth watching whether the September procedural vote actually materializes, versus treating the current rally as a durable regulatory-clarity repricing

signals.title: Beaten-down software names rebound as capital rotates out of AI hardware
signals.body: Salesforce, ServiceNow, Adobe, and other enterprise-software names have rallied sharply over the past one to two weeks as investors rotate profits out of richly valued AI-hardware winners and into software stocks that had fallen 30%+ this year on fears about AI's competitive threat. It's a notable shift from the wave of analyst downgrades that hit the sector earlier this summer, though it looks more like a sector-wide rotation than a change in the underlying AI-disruption debate.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether this rotation has legs or fades once AI-hardware names find their footing again

signals.title: CrowdStrike heads into earnings on a strong run; Zscaler cools off after its price-target rally
signals.body: CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks both hit record highs after this month's Black Hat conference highlighted rising AI-related security threats, and KeyBanc raised its CrowdStrike price target to $240 from $234 ahead of the company's Q2 report on August 26. Zscaler, meanwhile, pulled back today after last week's rally on fresh KeyBanc and Mizuho price-target hikes.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether CrowdStrike's earnings confirm the bullish setup or the sector gives back some of its recent gains on a mixed report

signals.title: China's humanoid-robotics space keeps drawing speculative capital despite today's pullback
signals.body: The Solactive China Humanoid Robotics Index is up roughly 75% over the past year, and UBTECH has gained more than 60% year-to-date, even as today's session saw the group broadly lower. Tesla has also leaned further into the theme, with its latest strategic roadmap emphasizing Optimus and Elon Musk suggesting the robot project could eventually account for a large share of the company's enterprise value.
signals.focus: worth treating single-day swings in individual robotics names as noise relative to the multi-year capital-flow trend into the space
